name: Watermelon — Order Intake & AI Assignment Pipeline

nodes.name: 🛒 Razorpay Payment Webhook
nodes.notes: Razorpay sends a POST to this URL when a payment is captured. Configure this URL in your Razorpay Dashboard → Webhooks → payment.captured event. The payload contains payment_id, order_id, and the metadata you attached at checkout (client details, service ID).

nodes.name: ✅ Verify Payment Event
nodes.notes: Razorpay sends many event types (payment.failed, refund.created, etc). We only proceed if the event is payment.captured — meaning money has actually landed. All other events fall through to the Ignore branch and return 200 OK silently.

nodes.name: 🔇 Ignore Non-Payment Events
nodes.notes: Return 200 OK immediately so Razorpay doesn't retry. We just don't process it further.

nodes.name: 🔍 Extract Payment Data
nodes.notes: Normalises the Razorpay payload into a clean flat object. Also converts paise to rupees (Razorpay stores ₹100 as 10000 paise — a common gotcha). Throws an error if supabase_order_id is missing so we catch bad integrations early.

nodes.name: 💾 Mark Order as PAID in Supabase
nodes.notes: Updates the order row status from 'pending' to 'paid'. Uses the Supabase REST API with the service role key (which bypasses RLS — only safe in server-side n8n, never in frontend). The Prefer: return=representation header makes Supabase return the updated row so the next step has the order data.

nodes.name: 🤖 Call AI Assignment Function
nodes.notes: Calls the ai_assign_order() PostgreSQL function we built in the schema. This single RPC call does everything inside one database transaction: finds the best intern by load ratio, creates the parent task and all subtasks, inserts notifications for both client and intern, and returns the routing log JSON. If anything fails, Postgres rolls back — no partial state.

nodes.name: 📊 Parse Assignment Result
nodes.notes: Merges the AI assignment result with the payment data collected earlier. Formats the delivery date in human-readable en-IN locale (e.g. '20 May 2026') and prepares the portal deep link. This merged object feeds both the WhatsApp and email nodes below.

parameters.name: Body

nodes.name: 💬 WhatsApp to Client
nodes.notes: Sends the client a WhatsApp confirmation via Twilio's WhatsApp Business API. The message includes the order ID, amount, assigned team member name, exact delivery date, and a direct link to their Client Portal order page. This is the moment that makes Watermelon feel like Flipkart — the client gets this within 5 seconds of paying.

parameters.name: Body

nodes.name: 📣 WhatsApp to Ops Team
nodes.notes: A parallel alert to your ops team WhatsApp number (or group). This means even before anyone opens the dashboard, the right people know a new order has landed and been assigned. Critical for the first few months when you want eyes on every order.

nodes.name: 📝 Log WhatsApp in Supabase
nodes.notes: Writes an audit record to the whatsapp_log table. Stores the Twilio message SID (provider_id) so you can check delivery status later. This log is visible to admin in the ops dashboard and is essential for debugging when a client says 'I never received a WhatsApp'.

nodes.name: ✉️ Build Email HTML
nodes.notes: Builds a full HTML email using inline styles (required for Gmail/Outlook compatibility — both strip <style> tags). The email mirrors the WhatsApp message but adds visual hierarchy with the green order details box and a CTA button linking to the Client Portal.

nodes.name: 📧 Send Confirmation Email
nodes.notes: Sends the HTML email via your configured SMTP provider (Resend, SendGrid, or Gmail SMTP all work). Set up credentials in n8n → Credentials → SMTP. For production, Resend.com gives you 3,000 free emails/month and excellent deliverability.

nodes.name: 🧾 Auto-Create Invoice
nodes.notes: Creates an invoice record in Supabase automatically. Note the GST calculation — 18% GST is added on top of the base amount. The invoice_number is auto-generated by the database trigger (INV-2026-XXXXXX). The client will see this in their portal's Invoices tab immediately.

}

nodes.name: ✅ Return Success to Razorpay
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 200 to Razorpay. This is critical — if you don't respond within 5 seconds, Razorpay will retry the webhook up to 8 times, potentially creating duplicate orders. The response contains the assignment summary for your own debugging.

nodes.name: 🔔 Invoice Ready Notification
nodes.notes: Inserts an in-app notification row so the client's portal shows 'Your invoice is ready' in real time via Supabase Realtime. Since the notifications table has REPLICA IDENTITY FULL and is in the Realtime publication, this row insert pushes a WebSocket event to the client's browser instantly.

nodes.name: ⏰ Monthly Renewal Check (1st of Month, 9AM)
nodes.notes: Runs at 9:00 AM on the 1st of every month. Checks for monthly subscriptions due for renewal in the next 14 days and sends reminder WhatsApp messages. This is the subscription management arm of the workflow — completely separate from the order intake arm above.

nodes.name: 📋 Fetch Upcoming Renewals
nodes.notes: Queries Supabase for all active monthly subscriptions with next_billing_date within the next 14 days. Uses PostgREST's join syntax (profiles!client_id, services!service_id) to get client and service names in a single request — no separate lookups needed.

nodes.name: 🔄 Split Renewals (One per Iteration)
nodes.notes: Splits the array of renewal-due orders so each one is processed individually in the loop below. This prevents rate limiting on the WhatsApp API and ensures each client gets a personalised message, not a batch.

nodes.name: 💬 WhatsApp Renewal Reminder
nodes.notes: Sends a personalised renewal reminder 14 days before the billing date. The 'Reply STOP to cancel' line is both a legal requirement and good practice — it gives clients a clear opt-out path, which paradoxically reduces cancellations because clients feel in control.

nodes.name: 📊 Weekly Health Score Refresh (Mon 8AM)
nodes.notes: Runs every Monday at 8AM. Finds all at-risk clients (health score < 75) and alerts the ops team. This is the churn prevention arm — your team lead gets a WhatsApp list of at-risk accounts every Monday morning so they can proactively reach out.

nodes.name: ⚠️ Fetch At-Risk Clients
nodes.notes: Fetches all clients with at_risk=true from the client_health view, ordered by score ascending (worst first). Joins with profiles to get the business name and phone number for the alert message.

nodes.name: 📝 Build Health Alert Message
nodes.notes: Aggregates all at-risk clients into a single WhatsApp message. If no clients are at risk, sets skip=true and the next IF node will stop the workflow here without sending anything — preventing unnecessary WhatsApp messages on good weeks.

nodes.name: ⚠️ Send At-Risk Alert to Ops
nodes.notes: Sends the consolidated at-risk report to your ops team WhatsApp. Every Monday morning your team lead wakes up to either silence (all good) or a prioritised list of clients to call that day.

main.node: 💾 Mark Order as PAID in Supabase

environment_variables_required: SUPABASE_URL              — Your project URL from Supabase Settings > API
SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY      — Service role key (NOT anon key) from Settings > API
TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN         — From Twilio Console dashboard (used as HTTP Basic password)
TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM      — Your Twilio WhatsApp sender, e.g. +14155238886
OPS_TEAM_PHONE            — Your team's WhatsApp number, e.g. +919876500000
APP_URL                   — Your deployed app URL, e.g. https://watermelon.in
import_instructions: 1. Open your n8n instance (self-hosted on Hostinger VPS)
2. Click the ≡ menu → Import from File
4. Go to Settings → Environment Variables and add all variables above
5. Add Twilio credentials: n8n Credentials → HTTP Basic Auth (username=AccountSID, password=AuthToken)
6. Configure SMTP credentials for the email node (recommend Resend.com)
7. Copy the Webhook node URL and paste it in Razorpay Dashboard → Webhooks
9. Click Activate on the workflow — it is now live
three_workflows_in_one: ARM 1 — Order Intake (webhook-triggered): Razorpay payment → Extract data → Mark paid → AI assign → WhatsApp client → WhatsApp ops → Email → Invoice → Notification
ARM 2 — Renewal Reminders (cron, 1st of month 9AM): Fetch upcoming renewals → Split → WhatsApp reminder per client
ARM 3 — Health Alerts (cron, every Monday 8AM): Fetch at-risk clients → Build alert → WhatsApp ops team
